kind: Research/test and correction of false provenance comment; no product behavior change
question: Can the F local successful pointer completion be removed and its C callers linked directly to original SIM32?
conclusion: Not by link-only substitution: WOW direct mappings do not imply SIM32 scratch ownership, and ABI differs. Keep ID open; no B no-op relocation or new state machine.

evidence.selection: Pinned OpenNT softpc.h line471 TRUE macro is under i386. Selected non-i386 declaration is line535. Current mirror retains this external declaration.
evidence.CPU: ccpusas4.c c_sas_overwrite_memory is an intentional empty CCPU no-compiled-cache notification. This does not erase SIM32 video writeback.
evidence.WOW: GetPModeVDMPointerAssert uses FlatAddress after original selector validation/fault-in. DpmiSetDescriptorEntry sets FlatAddress from GetDescriptorMapping or IntelBase+base. This is not Sim32pGetVDMPointer/GetVideoMemory pairing.
evidence.SIM32: Original sim32.c converts selector/real address; video targets require ScratchVideoBuffer and SetVideoMemory writes the remaining aperture from its snapshot, ignoring buff/size as transfer source/extent.
evidence.ABI: Current WOW map resolves _Sim32FlushVDMPointer@16 locally; worker original resolves _Sim32FlushVDMPointer cdecl, already exported at44. No blind decorated alias.
evidence.runtime: Existing real CCPU fixture, linked original sim32.obj: RAM success; missing scratch FALSE; paired scratch writeback succeeds; direct writes followed by flush are overwritten from old scratch, including a second byte outside size=1. Full existing bounded/high-linear/lease checks still pass.
